messages:
zoe: Quick heads-up — saw a spike of 413s on /embeddings when customers send mixed-dim vectors in a single payload. Minimal thread: can we decide whether router should pre-validate dims or rely on the splitter?

ian: I looked at traces — splitter currently decides by bytes and target-shard capacity. If dims don't match a shard profile it returns 413 instead of splitting, which surfaces as a hard error upstream.

sumit: This is partly quota interplay — we treat some shard limits as hard at the router to avoid overcommit, but that prevents graceful auto-splitting.

priya: From console/UX POV we get a bunch of support tickets asking for clearer guidance. Suggestion: console preflight should show estimated shard count + "likely failure reason" before the request is sent. Also an "auto-split" toggle for teams who prefer us to split on their behalf. :thinking_face:

tom: Proposal: add two optional headers so SDKs/clients can hint dims and item count: 
```
X-Vector-Dims: 1536
X-Vector-Count: 512
```
Router can use those for fast validation and nicer errors instead of opaque 413.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: embed-splitter service v1.3 -> 5% traffic to canary pool (region-us).

ian: Telemetry needs: per-request dims histogram, split_decision_count, dropped_by_quota_count, split_latency_ms, and which shard-type was selected. We need these in Console traces + metrics to debug.

sumit: Agreed. Also add a metric for "auto-split_fallbacks" so we can see when splitter had to downshift quality for capacity reasons.

zoe: One design question — should router prefer low-latency, lower-capacity shards for tiny batches (single small-dim vectors) instead of grouping them to a high-throughput shard? Tradeoffs: latency vs cost efficiency.

priya: Product input — users care about predictable latency for interactive embeddings. If we can surface a per-route SLO in Console and let teams opt into "latency-first" routing that could be a nice feature. But pricing messaging must be clear.

tom: On error semantics: 413 is technically correct for payload too large, but it's not actionable. I'm in favor of returning 400 with a structured error that includes fields: expected_dims, detected_dims, suggested_split_count. SDKs can then auto-split.

ian: That works. We'll keep 413 for infra-level rejections (malformed) but for routing/size issues return 400+structured body. Also log the raw decision id so support can correlate.

sumit: Rough timeline: I can ship telemetry + structured errors in next sprint. Auto-split behavior (with heuristics for mixed dims) will be a 2-sprint project. I'll create tickets and link them.

zoe: Assignments: @sumit telemetry + tickets, @tom header validation + error shape, @priya console preflight UX + "auto-split" toggle design. I'll open a short RFC and schedule a 30m sync for tomorrow. :thumbsup:

priya: Nice. I'll add mockups to the RFC and include a quick console trace mock showing suggested shard counts.

ian: I'll add the additional metrics to the tracing middleware and include a trace tag: `split_decision_id`.

zoe: Thanks team — let's converge on the RFC today so we can start the canary next week.
